findings: Source lines 13 and 17–50 accurately identify the May Hono/middleware quickstart and need explicit historical scope. The November guide’s intended diagram shows HTTP 402, a client retry with a credential, facilitator verification and on-chain settlement, Stripe recording with a confirmed PaymentIntent returned to the server, then delivery to the client. The example protects the route through verification and facilitator settlement. Its separate onAfterSettle hook requires result.success and a transaction hash, requests confirmation of a crypto transaction_verification PaymentIntent using allowed_payment_method_types and the hash as its idempotency key, and logs the Intent ID without an explicit Stripe status or recovery check. These passages do not establish an independently verified recording gate, delivery or exactly-once outcome (old raw lines 30–51 and 139–183, new raw lines 24–39, 112–136 and 151–189).

New raw: `raw/stripe-payments-machine-x402-2026-11-07.md`. Prior raw: `raw/stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart-2026.md`. Current summaries: `wiki/sources/source-stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart.md`.

- Q1: For `https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/x402`, what central documented behavior, prerequisites, identities and state boundaries does the complete new capture establish, and how does it compare with the matched old capture and every mapped current summary?

- Q2: Which changes are substantive versus presentational or navigation-only? Which historical claims must remain dated, which conflicts need reciprocal warnings, and which API, UI, version, client/server or outcome qualifications prevent unsupported inferences?

reviewed_answers.Q1: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/x402, the November guide describes HTTP 402 with a Stripe deposit address, an authorized client retry, and facilitator verification and on-chain settlement. Its intended lifecycle diagram places Stripe’s confirmed PaymentIntent response before resource delivery (new raw lines 24-39). The worked Base mainnet route charges a fixed 0.01 USD in USDC, uses an authenticated CDP facilitator and a precreated Stripe deposit address as static payTo, and protects delivery with facilitator verification and settlement (new raw lines 54-87, new raw lines 103-136). The separate onAfterSettle hook requires result.success and a transaction hash, requests confirmation of a crypto transaction_verification PaymentIntent with the hash as its idempotency key, and logs its ID without an explicit Stripe status or recovery check. The example does not establish an independently verified successful recording gate, delivery or exactly-once outcome (new raw lines 151-189). The guide requires approved Stablecoins and Crypto access and documents the New York exception and a request path in 30+ countries outside the US (new raw lines 13-22). The May quickstart used 2026-03-04.preview to create an upfront deposit-mode PaymentIntent, reused validated cached retry addresses and illustrated Base Sepolia (old raw lines 18-51, old raw lines 103-183, old raw lines 186-210). source-stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart.md lines 13–50 describe the May approach and omit the November address, recording, access and environment boundaries.
reviewed_answers.Q2: At https://docs.stripe.com/payments/machine/x402, substantive changes are the precreated static Base recipient, post-settlement transaction_verification record, CDP Base mainnet walkthrough, access wording and separate sandbox versus live test paths. The coding-agent prompt, links and formatting are guidance and presentation. Preserve the May 2026-03-04.preview dynamic deposit-mode quickstart and the May sibling's deposit-mode simulator and auto-capture guidance as dated, and add reciprocal warnings in source-stripe-machine-payments-x402-quickstart.md and the Stripe Machine Payments concept. In November, 2026-05-27.preview appears for live address creation and is stated for recording, while sandbox address creation shows 2026-07-29.preview. Live purl moves real funds. Sandbox uses Base Sepolia test USDC and a public facilitator without CDP signup. The transaction_verification PaymentIntent table lists Tempo, Base and Solana. Its Tempo USDC row shows 0x20c000000000000000000000b9537d11c60e8b50 (new raw lines 216-224). The separate Tempo create-deposit-address reference shows 0x20c0000000000000000000009e8d7eb59b783726 with token_currency usdc in a livemode:false example (raw/stripe-api-crypto-deposit-address-create-2026-11-07.md:11-15,18-34). Mark those operations and examples on the reciprocal route. The Machine Payments protocol table lists Tempo MPP USDC.e, while the x402 walkthrough is Base USDC and directs card acceptance to MPP (raw/stripe-payments-machine-2026-11-07.md:41-49, new raw lines 9-11, new raw lines 107-123). The captures do not establish token migration, interchangeable contracts or availability in an uninspected environment. The old New York and Texas/US-only availability claims should stay with their May authorities, and the later request route does not prove account approval. A chain settlement and recording response do not establish balance availability, payout or exact-once delivery (old raw lines 18-51, old raw lines 53-71, old raw lines 112-183, new raw lines 9-22, new raw lines 24-39, new raw lines 54-74, new raw lines 141-189, new raw lines 192-281).
